probe: Test r269's next alternative: whether one O(1)-active-state retained predecessor digest or hash-chain anchor can mechanically detect authoritative-ref rewrite or terminal deletion, without branch-protection/admin authority, hosted compute, finite quota, a shared rolling CAS hotspot, or same-run retry.
result: FALSIFIED_UNCONDITIONALLY; CONDITIONAL_DETECTION_ONLY. A retained predecessor digest can detect the first terminal deletion or ref rollback only if the anchor itself survives in a retention domain not subject to the same rewrite and the anchored prior snapshot remains retrievable. If terminal P and the only O(1) anchor are both mutable under the rewritten authoritative ref, there exist two histories—P never created, versus P created then the ref and co-resident anchor rewound—that yield the same later observable state. No deterministic recurrence can distinguish those histories. A hash-chain root on the same ref therefore does not remove r269's monotonic-retention requirement; it merely compresses retained evidence. An independently retained prior commit SHA plus terminal-path lookup can fail closed after detecting deletion, but this detects rather than prevents loss and remains conditional on independent anchor survival and prior-snapshot retrievability.

model.world_never_created: At recurrence t2 the authoritative ref R2 contains no terminal path P and exposes current role-local anchor A2.
model.world_created_then_rewritten: At t0 P existed and an anchor committed to it; between t0 and t2 the authoritative ref is force-moved/reset or rewritten to the same R2 while any co-resident mutable anchor is rewound to A2. The t2 current-ref/path observations are identical to world_never_created.
model.indistinguishability_consequence: When all evidence available to the detector is stored in the same rewrite domain, the two histories have identical t2 observations, so exact prior-existence detection is impossible regardless of the hash function or chain layout.
surviving_anchor_case: Retain O(1) anchor E=(prior_snapshot_sha, prior_anchor_digest) outside the rewrite domain.
If current deterministic terminal path P is absent, query P at prior_snapshot_sha. A matching prior terminal proves deletion/rollback and the recurrence must fail closed rather than recreate.
If prior_snapshot_sha or E is unavailable, rewritten, or no longer retrievable, the detector returns unresolved; it cannot infer never-created.
This mechanism detects a divergence after it occurred; it does not prevent the terminal record from being removed.
model.hash_chain_limit: A constant-size current hash-chain root alone cannot answer arbitrary prior terminal-membership questions after deletion unless a membership witness, retrievable prior snapshot/history, or equivalent retained evidence survives. Moving that witness/history outside the rewritten ref reintroduces an independent retention assumption.
model.git_ref_observation: GitHub's documented refs API permits a reference update to a supplied SHA and exposes a force flag; force=false enforces fast-forward behavior for that update, while force=true permits a non-fast-forward move. GitHub's commit API accepts a commit SHA as a commit reference for reads. These capabilities support conditional detection from a surviving prior SHA but do not establish immutable or indefinitely retained snapshots without a separate retention guarantee.

tested_scope: One bounded CLEAN architecture/information-flow falsification using frozen current controls, own r269 LATEST/checkpoint, and public GitHub API documentation. The model covers one deterministic terminal P, one retained predecessor digest/snapshot anchor, one rewrite/removal event, and one later recurrence. It distinguishes detection from prevention. It does not claim GitHub guarantees indefinite retention of unreachable commits or immutable refs. No O/downstream/other-worker semantics, protected authority, hosted compute/storage add-ons, external model/API execution, finite monthly/trial/paid quota consumption, manual execution, scheduler mutation, same-run wait/poll/backoff/retry, or optional second leaf was used.
conflict_check: Exactly one bounded CLEAN Phase-1 child was executed. Exact-blob two-pass DESIRED_STATE/config authority matched. Only own role-local state and own receipt namespaces are authorized for mutation; no scheduler or protected authority mutation occurred.
frontier: r269's monotonic terminal-retention condition is information-theoretically necessary whenever all active evidence is subject to the same ref rewrite domain.
An O(1) hash-chain root compresses evidence but cannot by itself preserve prior-existence knowledge across rollback of the root itself.
A surviving prior snapshot SHA plus one retained digest is enough to detect the first divergence and fail closed, but only under an independent anchor/snapshot-retention assumption.
Detection is not prevention: exact duplicate/no-silent-loss safety remains conditional unless at least one evidence channel is monotonic relative to the destructive rewrite being modeled.
exact_continuation: Fresh-bootstrap current controls and reconstruct r270 from LATEST. Execute exactly one bounded CLEAN Phase-1 child: test whether a dedicated second Git ref updated only with non-force fast-forward semantics can serve as the independent O(1) anchor without branch-protection/admin authority. Model protocol-compliant concurrent Chat writers plus one stale writer, then separately model any actor able to force-move either ref. Determine the exact threat-model boundary: whether two refs eliminate shared-CAS/duplicate risk for protocol participants while exact rollback detection still fails against force-capable rewrite, and preserve the next zero-quota alternative without broadening scope.
